course_name_original: Experimentation and simulation of energy systems
course_name_en: Experimentation and simulation of energy systems
prerequisites: A basic knowledge of fundamentals of Mathematics, Physics Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics and Energy Systems is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge relating to the design of the experimentation (even virtual) on Energy Systems and the interpretation of the obtained results.
Acquire skills concerning the numerical and experimental characterization of Energy Systems operations.
Acquire tools for the implementation, execution and analysis of models for the simulation of Energy Systems and for the interpretation of simulation results.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of energy conversion systems (turbogas, steam plants and internal combustion engines) and their components with IT tools to determine performance as operating conditions vary.
Main problems related to the experimental characterization of energy systems and fluid machines.
Instruments and sensors typically used in test cells.
Procedures to perform test-bench experiments under steady-state conditions.
Procedures to perform test-bench experiments under transient conditions.
Use of virtual environments for the simulation and modeling of energy systems.
Numerical solution of engineering problems through physical–mathematical modeling (calculation of thermodynamic transformations, analysis of energy systems).
Investigation of the effect of the main control parameters on system performance through virtual experimentation.
Generation of reports that clearly and technically present the results of the analyses performed.
teaching_methods: Classroom exercises (students are invited to participate with a computer)

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam consisting of the discussion of a report outlining the exercises proposed in the classroom and carried out independently by the individual student

assessment_rules: The exam is oral and consists of the discussion of a report outlining the exercises proposed in the classroom and carried out independently by the individual student. No specific grading formula or minimum marks are stated.
